style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: matte clay 3D render of a small mechanical assembly resting on a real textured surface in a real space. The assembly features an intricate, modular looping track mechanism running endlessly, with a distinct, heavy-duty gating barrier positioned physically outside the loop's path, failing to intersect it. Recognisable engineered parts: a circular track module, a disconnected block housing, and an unlatched gate cover. Matte surfaces with visible moulding seams and contact shadows resting on weathered brushed steel. Asymmetrical off-centre layout with heavy editorial margin on the right. One directional key light raking across them, throwing a long cast shadow. Matte muted palette with one bright amber accent on the gate. Minimalist composition, generous empty margin.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, typography, watermarks, signatures
rationale: A clay render is ideal for illustrating abstract, structural news like software loops and missing bounds. By depicting an engineered, repeating track assembly (the loop) missing a crucial barrier, it captures the 'runaway' concept physically without relying on literal datacenter cliches.
cue: 68 loops that nothing in the code stopped
subject: a mechanical looping track assembly missing a gate
core_thesis: Agentic AI loops can run endlessly and exhaust resources without external bounds, as default frameworks often fail to stop them.
core_conflict: Unchecked autonomous agent loops vs. rigid external control limits
composition: asymmetrical off-centre layout with heavy editorial margin
alt_text: Unstoppable Agent Loops. A modular looping track mechanism with an unattached barrier resting on brushed steel.
